bridges.name: Euclidean vector norms and normalization
bridges.content_boundary: Define the Euclidean norm, normalize a non-zero vector, and recognize zero-vector breakdown; exclude general normed-space theory.

learning_outcomes.text: Compute the Euclidean norm of a real vector.
Normalize a non-zero vector and verify that the result has unit Euclidean norm.
Recognize that the zero vector cannot be normalized by division by its norm.

teaching_content.text: For x = (x_1, ..., x_n)^T in R^n, the Euclidean norm is ||x||_2 = sqrt(x_1^2 + ... + x_n^2) = sqrt(x^T x).
For x != 0, compute r = ||x||_2 and set u = x/r. Then ||u||_2 = 1.
If ||x||_2 = 0, then x is the zero vector and x/||x||_2 is undefined; stop before dividing.
For x = (3, 4)^T, ||x||_2 = 5 and the normalized vector is (3/5, 4/5)^T.

sources.title: Vector Norms and Normalization
sources.evidence_locator: Chapter 1, vector length/norm passage: Euclidean length formula and unit-vector normalization; the normalization discussion states the vector must be nonzero and identifies division by the zero norm as undefined.

bridges.name: Orthogonality, orthonormal bases, and projection coefficients
bridges.content_boundary: Use inner products to explain orthogonality, orthonormal bases, and scalar projection coefficients v_i^T x; exclude the spectral theorem and eigenbasis expansion because those belong to RC-003 and RC-006.

learning_outcomes.text: Test whether two real vectors are orthogonal using their inner product.
Recognize an orthonormal family from zero cross-products and unit norms.
Compute the scalar coefficient v^T x when v is a unit vector.

teaching_content.text: Real vectors u and v are orthogonal when u^T v = 0.
Vectors v_1, ..., v_k are orthonormal when v_i^T v_j = 0 for i != j and ||v_i||_2 = 1.
For a unit vector v, calculate v^T x to obtain the scalar coefficient of x in the v direction.
For v = (1, 0)^T and x = (3, 4)^T, v^T x = 3.

sources.title: Orthogonal vectors and subspaces
sources.evidence_locator: Chapter 5, orthogonality and orthonormal vectors passage: zero inner products define orthogonality and unit mutually orthogonal vectors are orthonormal.

sources.title: Orthogonal projections and least squares
sources.evidence_locator: Chapter 4, projection coefficient passage: for a unit direction v, the scalar coefficient is v^T x; worked calculation uses v=(1,0)^T and x=(3,4)^T.

bridges.name: Inner products and quadratic forms
bridges.content_boundary: Compute x^T A x, x^T x, and compatible scalar-vector expressions used by the Rayleigh quotient and residual; exclude general quadratic-form classification.

learning_outcomes.text: Compute x^T y and identify the scalar result.
Compute x^T A x by forming Ax and then taking the inner product with x.
Relate x^T x to the squared Euclidean norm without classifying general quadratic forms.

teaching_content.text: For real vectors x and y of the same length, x^T y is the dot product and is the scalar sum of componentwise products.
To compute x^T A x, first compute y = Ax and then compute the scalar x^T y. Check that A is square and compatible with x.
The special case x^T x equals ||x||_2^2 and is non-negative.

excluded_content: Derivation or interpretation of the Rayleigh quotient

sources.title: Vector norms, dot products, and lengths
sources.evidence_locator: Chapter 1, dot-product and length passage: x^T y is the dot product and x^T x equals the square of the Euclidean length ||x||_2^2.

sources.title: Positive Definite Matrices and Minima: Problem 27.2 Solution
sources.evidence_locator: Problem 27.2 solution demonstrates forming Ax and computing the scalar x^T A x, including the compatible matrix-vector dimensions.

bridges.name: Basic NumPy vector operations
bridges.content_boundary: Use array conversion, shape inspection, matrix-vector multiplication, norms, comparisons, exceptions, and tuple returns needed by the Contract implementation; exclude unrelated NumPy APIs.

learning_outcomes.text: Convert compatible inputs to floating-point NumPy arrays and inspect their shapes.
Use @ for matrix-vector multiplication and numpy.linalg.norm for vector norms.
Read simple comparison, exception, and tuple-return patterns used by the Contract implementation.

teaching_content.text: Convert inputs with A = np.asarray(A, dtype=float) and x = np.asarray(x0, dtype=float), then inspect A.shape and x.shape before arithmetic.
For a two-dimensional array A and one-dimensional array x with compatible dimensions, y = A @ x computes the matrix-vector product.
Use n = np.linalg.norm(x) for the default Euclidean norm of a one-dimensional vector and test n == 0.0 before dividing by n.

Use explicit shape or value checks and raise a specific exception for invalid input; comparisons on arrays are elementwise, so reduce or compare scalar diagnostics when a single truth value is required.
A function may return several diagnostics as one tuple, for example return value, vector, iterations, residual; callers can unpack the tuple into four names.

excluded_content: Vectorization or broadcasting beyond the required operations
